targets.title: Testing the death thought suppression and rebound hypothesis: Death thought accessibility following mortality salience decreases during a delay.
targets.evidence_quote:
We present results from 22
labs in 11 countries (total N = 3,447) attempting to replicate and extend an existing study of TMT, Study 3 from Trafimow
and Hughes, and the role of time-delay effects.
targets.outcome_quote:
We successfully replicate Trafimow and Hughes and demonstrate that it is
possible to prime death-related thoughts and that priming is more effective when there is no delay between the priming
and outcome measure.
targets.outcome_reasoning: The authors explicitly give an overall successful replication verdict for Study 3.

reasoning: New participants across 22 laboratories retest Study 3 from one published paper; other TMT citations contextualize the finding.
